text:
Maya (Sales): Quick sync — Prospect (Acadia Health) wants to kick off a Dedicated POC but sent DPA redlines asking for explicit KMS attestation, SOC2 evidence, and requested Net60 on the PO. Their security team also blocks DocuSign outbound calls. Need to finalize MSA + order form and confirm signature path. What can we deliver without delaying the POC start?

Priya (Legal): Paste the exact DPA redline if possible. High-level: we can add a one-page KMS addendum saying we will provide an attestation or HSM certificate within X business days. Need to limit attestation scope to keys used for their tenant. For signatures: we can accept signed PDFs uploaded to our secure portal with email confirmation + hash stored in audit log. Wet-ink only if >$250k or regulated entity requires it.

Maya (Sales): Redline snippet: "Customer may require KMS attestation and audit access to key metadata; Vendor must provide such attestation prior to production use."

Priya (Legal): Proposed language: "Upon Customer request, Vendor will provide a KMS/HSM attestation limited to the cryptographic material used for Customer's environment. Vendor will deliver a signed attestation or certificate within 7 business days of a written request, unless Customer requests on-prem validation, which requires a separate SOW." That keeps timeline tight.

Carlos (Finance): Net60 adds risk. For POCs under $20k we can do Net30 standard. If they insist on Net60 we need CFO approval and either: 1) a $25k refundable hold, or 2) milestone-based billing (50% upfront). Also require PO number on invoice and remit coordinates.

Ravi (Infra): Operational note: generating an HSM attestation requires us to run our attest flow and sign with our portal cert. Typical turnaround is 3 business days if scope is limited. If they want a full on-prem KMS inspection that becomes a 6-8 week project. Also DocuSign: we can provide a hosted signing link delivered to them (same as DocuSign flow) but if they block DocuSign egress we'll need them to whitelist our signing IP or accept portal uploads.

doc-bot: Uploaded: https://secure.docs/redwood/Acadia/acadia_dpa_redline_v1.pdf — created checklist: [KMS addendum draft] [Net terms approval] [Signature fallback confirmed] [SOC2 link sent]

Maya (Sales): I'll ask if they can temporarily whitelist our signing IP 3.24.18.0/24 for the PO window. If not, portal upload is acceptable per Priya. I'll also ask whether Net60 is required for enterprise procurement or just a preference.

Priya (Legal): I'll draft the KMS addendum and include the 7 business day attestation commitment + scope limit clause. Also add portal-upload signature language: "Signed PDF uploaded to Vendor secure portal with audit trail and mirrored email confirmation shall constitute \"signed\" for all purposes."

Carlos (Finance): If PO estimate is $18k as Maya mentioned in the thread with procurement, we approve Net30. If they revise to Net60, route to me and I'll request CFO signoff and a $25k hold.

Ravi (Infra): Note for onboarding timeline: once contracts are countersigned and KMS attestation request is received, Dedicated POC provisioning is ~14 business days. On-prem HSM or installation checks will add weeks. Also we will need tenant-level SSO access to validate key usage patterns — include in onboarding checklist.

Maya (Sales): Sounds good. Actions: 1) I'll confirm PO amount and request DocuSign IP whitelist or portal upload, 2) Priya will send KMS addendum, 3) Carlos will confirm finance path if Net60 required, 4) Ravi to prepare attestation flow.

Priya (Legal): Drafting addendum now and will post link when ready.

Maya (Sales): Thanks — I'll update after procurement responds. :raised_hands:
